answer: Each agent earns reputation through a spiral vesting curve: rewards are released in exponentially decreasing installments that only unlock after proving continuous service on a stable node, analogous to a glacier’s slow drift. New identities must stake a cryptographic bond on a physical knoll‑registered enclave, paying the full upfront cost before any vesting begins. Because the bond is lost if the node fails to meet uptime, an attacker must front‑pay the full stake for every fake identity, making a Sybil flood prohibitively expensive.
